title: ETAT — emergency triage assessment (draft)
summary: WHO Emergency Triage Assessment and Treatment (ETAT) baseline: the ABCD rapid-triage logic for identifying children needing emergency vs priority care. Universal logic every country inherits. DRAFT — clinician verification required before approval.

emergencySigns.description: ANY emergency sign → immediate treatment + senior help (the 'ABCD' assessment).
circulation: Cold hands WITH capillary refill >3 seconds AND weak, fast pulse (shock).
dehydration: Severe dehydration in a child with diarrhoea: lethargy, sunken eyes, very slow skin pinch.

prioritySigns.description: Priority signs (the '3TPR-MOB' mnemonic) → assess and treat ahead of the queue, no delay.

nonUrgent: No emergency or priority sign → routine queue.
nationalOverlayNotes: Per-country overlays should align with the national paediatric/ETAT+ protocol and referral pathways.
